newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, Nov 19 - Haifa - Fifteen vessels operating of which 8 discharging (6 general cargo, 2 bulkers), 4 containers, 2 tankers, 1 passenger vessel. 3 Vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge (1 general cargo, 2 bulkers). 2 Vessels bunkering, 2 under repair/dry-docked, 2 awaiting orders. 3 Vessels due, with 1-2 days delay expected. Ashdod - Twelve vessels operating of which 7 discharging general cargo, 4 containers, 1 passenger vessel, 1 bulker waiting at anchorage, 1-2 days berthing delay expected. Eilat - Two vessels operating of which 1 bulker loading, 1 passenger vessel. 1 Bulker waiting at anchorage to load.

MOZAMBIQUE - Nov 18 - Acala - Port working normally on a first come-first served basis. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally on a first come-first served basis. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally. Pilotage now possle 24 hours per day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. Maputo - Pilotage now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 120 metres loa with a maximum draft of 9 metres. Two tugs (one out of order). Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangement with the port captain. All berths are working normally and expected to remain so (first come-first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres plus the rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, November 18 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, Nov 18 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths, congested with berthing delays of up to 48 hours experienced at present and likely to continue until beginning of December. Bulk import berths working normally. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.), working normally. Bulk coal berths considerable congestion of vessels awaiting berthing turns at present, delays of approx. 3 days being experienced. Fourteen vessels anchored with a further 14 due this week. Berthing delays of approx. 3 days expected for the remainder of the week. Durban - Container terminal delays of up to 36 hours being experienced at present. Point/New Pier/Maydon wharf berths working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) two sunflower loaders for November. Bunker supplies fluid. Delays of up to 4 hours in supplying bunkers can be expected due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock, fully booked for November.

East London - General cargo-combi terminal berths extremely busy but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock fully booked for November and December, thereafter open for bookings. Copper moving in small parcels of 2,500 tonnes per month in containers to the Far East. Gas oil pipeline under utilised. Wheat imports, two vessels due mid-December. Log loaders, one vessel due end-November. Scrap steel, one vessel in port to lift 17,000 tonnes. Tankers, expected to be busy until end December. Port Elizabeth - Port working normally with 4 vessels in port. No delays expected on general or tanker berths. Ore berth, one loader due 20/11 and another 21/11. A delay of approx. 28 hours was expected for the second loader. Container berth, three vessels due p.m. 9/11 with 1 experiencing approx. 8 hours delay. A further two vessels are due 20/11 with berthing delays of 10-12 hours expected. One pool iron loader expected end-November and 2 scrap loaders early December.

Cape Town - Breakbulk berths, no delays expected for coming week. Container terminal, although major delays experienced due to wind, the terminal does not foresee any major delays for the coming week. Bunker berths, a delay of 16-24 hours can be expected due to 9 vessels arriving today. Dry-docks, repair quay, fully occupied at present, with booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Nov 16 - Gabes - Two vessels loading at berth. 1 Discharging at berth (bulk sulphur). 1 Bulk fertiliser vessel waiting at anchor to load, 1 vessel under arrest. Sousse - One vessel discharging bagged sugar, no waiting time. Tunis - Five vessels in port of which 1 discharging potatoes, 1 marble blocks, 3 general cargo. Rades - Three ro/ro vessels, 1 vessel discharging containers. La Goulette - North side, 1 passenger vessel, 1 vessel dredging, 1 cereal vessel. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 motor tanker. Styrene - 2 Vessels in roads awaiting cereal berth. Nov 18 - Bizerte - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. Three vessels in port of which 1 discharging fuel oil, 1 coke, 1 loading clinker. Zarzis - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. No vessels in port.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Nov 10-16 - Dubai - 176 vessels of which 73 containers, 9 general cargo, 6 general cargo/containers, 3 bulk carriers, 5 car carriers, 15 tankers, 8 naval vessels, 4 UAE Naval vessels, 1 livestock carrier, 3 taking bunkers/stores/under repair, 6 dhows, 10 barges, 8 tugs, 20 supply boats, 1 NGL lifter, 1 heavy lift, 2 refrigerator vessels, 1 rig.

YEMEN, Nov 18 - Hodeidah all berths occupied except no.8. Six vessels alongside of which 1 bulk wheat, 1 sugar, 2 steel, 1 container, 1 general cargo. No vessels anchored. Berthing delays general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargo up to 4 days, bulk cargo up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - Two vessels discharging alongside, 1 palm oil, 1 wheat flour. No vessels anchored, 48 hours berthing delay.
ZAIRE, Nov 14 - All ports are working normally.
